# `state/replication/CrossShardCoordinator.js`

> **Source:** `engine/state/replication/CrossShardCoordinator.js`

state/replication/CrossShardCoordinator.js — cross-domain atomic commit (spec §10, rule 40).  Cross-domain atomicity is the most expensive operation, so it is used only when true all-or-nothing behavior is required. This coordinator implements two-phase commit with the §10 hardening: • locks are acquired in CANONICAL order (sorted shard/key) to avoid deadlock; • a durable PREPARED record is written so a coordinator that crashes after prepare can be recovered and the commit completed (classic 2PC blocks on coordinator failure; the prepared record makes it recoverable); • for operations that do NOT need atomicity, a SAGA fallback is offered instead, since compensation is cheaper than distributed commit.

### `class CrossShardCoordinator`

| Method | Signature | Summary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `constructor(shardIds = [])` |  |
| `_shard` | `_shard(id)` |  |
| `read` | `read(shardId, key)` | Current committed value of a key on a shard. |
| `prepare` | `prepare(txId, ops = [])` | Phase 1 — PREPARE. Acquire all locks in canonical order; record a durable prepared entry. Returns failure (releasing any partial locks) on conflict. |
| `commit` | `commit(txId)` | Phase 2 — COMMIT. Apply all prepared ops atomically and release locks. |
| `abort` | `abort(txId)` | Abort a prepared transaction: discard the record and release its locks. |
| `isPrepared` | `isPrepared(txId)` | True if a tx is prepared but not yet committed (the in-doubt window). |
| `recover` | `recover(txId)` | Recover an in-doubt transaction after a coordinator crash by completing the commit from its durable prepared record — 2PC's blocking failure mode made recoverable. |
| `sagaFallback` | `async sagaFallback(steps, ctx = {})` | SAGA fallback for cross-shard work that does NOT require atomicity: run a sequence of local steps with compensation instead of a distributed commit. |
